transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… my husband thought I should come, mostly, because this whole kitchen situation has just gone on and on. We had a contractor, and for almost two years now I’ve been sure he and some people on our block are sort of working together—quietly, you know—to cheat us and keep things wrong on purpose.

I know that sounds like a lot when you say it out loud. But the cabinets don’t line up right, and every time there’s some new excuse. My husband keeps showing me receipts and saying it’s just delays or mistakes, but I don’t buy that. And the neighbors… they notice more than they let on. It reminds me of when my sister had trouble with her roof years ago, people always act like contractors are saints, but they know exactly what they’re doing. Anyway, that’s why I’m here.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Hearing voices? I mean… no, not like someone standing in the room talking to me when nobody’s there. I don’t think so. Sometimes I hear things outside, like a car door or people on the sidewalk, and then my husband says he didn’t hear it, but he never hears half the things in the house anyway—he’ll sit right through the refrigerator making that awful buzz.

But voices, no… I wouldn’t put it that way.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or needed much less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure what you’d call “unusually” energetic. I mean, I have days where I’m up doing things around the house, but then everybody does, don’t they? Especially when there’s something bothering you, like if the kitchen is a mess and you keep noticing little things that need fixing.

As for sleep… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve had some big stretch where I barely slept and felt wonderful or anything like that. I’m 67, sleep isn’t always perfect, but I wouldn’t say I suddenly needed hardly any.
Have you had any major medical illness affecting your brain, such as a stroke?

A stroke? No, I don’t think so… I mean, nobody’s ever told me I had something like that. I did have an aunt who had one, years ago, and after that everyone in the family started watching every little dizzy spell like it was a disaster waiting to happen.

But for me, no major brain illness that I know of. I’ve had the usual aches and things, but nothing like what you’re asking.
Do you ever feel that ordinary things happening around you—like the way neighbors look at you or small events on the street—carry a special message meant specifically for you?

Well… I don’t know if I’d say “special message,” exactly. It’s more that you start to notice things don’t add up. Like with the contractor—this has been going on nearly two years with the kitchen, and it’s still not right. And then certain people on the block, the way they act, the little looks, the timing of things… it feels like they know.

My husband keeps showing me receipts and saying, “See, it’s all accounted for,” but receipts can be made to look any way they want. People think if it’s on paper then that settles it, but it doesn’t. They give excuses, and somehow the kitchen stays half-wrong on purpose. So yes, ordinary things maybe aren’t so ordinary when you’ve been living with it this long.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t know… I still do some of the things I used to, when I feel like it. It’s just that things get interrupted, you know? If the house is unsettled, it’s hard to sit and enjoy a book or a program the way you used to.

But “losing interest”… I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Sometimes I start something and then remember there’s something else that needs checking, like a bill or a drawer that got moved around, and then the whole afternoon is gone. So I wouldn’t say I don’t enjoy things anymore, exactly. It’s more that there’s always something in the way.
Did this way of thinking about the contractor and neighbors come on suddenly for you?

No, not suddenly like waking up one morning and everything was different. It sort of built up… I’d say it’s been about a year and nine months now, since they started all that work on the kitchen and the garden and had the house turned upside down.

At first I thought, well, remodeling is always a mess—you know, my cousin had her bathroom done and they left dust in places you wouldn’t believe—but then little things kept happening, and it just didn’t settle down. So no, not all at once. It came along with all that disruption.
Have you been having problems with your memory?

Memory? I don’t think so… I mean, I forget why I walked into a room sometimes, but who doesn’t at my age? My sister used to do that even when she was younger, she’d open the refrigerator and just stand there like it was going to tell her what she wanted.

But no, I haven’t noticed anything serious. Sometimes I misplace things, but then again, when things in the house aren’t where I left them, that’s not necessarily my memory. So… I’m not sure what kind of memory problems you mean.
Has anyone told you that your speech or thoughts have become hard to follow or seem jumbled?

Hard to follow? I don’t think anyone’s said that to me, not in those words. Sometimes people act impatient, but people are impatient now anyway—my niece talks so fast on the phone, and then she says I’m not answering what she asked, but she asks three things at once.

I mean, I know I explain things because there’s background to it. You can’t just say, “the drawer was open,” without saying what had been in it before, otherwise it doesn’t make sense. But jumbled? No… I haven’t noticed that. What do you mean by jumbled exactly?
Have you felt that other people can know your thoughts, as if your thoughts are no longer private?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes people look at you in a way where you wonder what they think they know, but that’s not the same as them hearing what’s in my head.

Thoughts being private—well, they should be, shouldn’t they? My mother used to say you can think whatever you like as long as you don’t say it at the dinner table. But no, I haven’t had the feeling that someone can actually know my thoughts like that. What exactly do you mean, like reading them?
Have you been smelling things that other people don’t seem to notice?

Smelling things? No, I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes the kitchen has a funny smell, but that’s usually the garbage or something in the sink. My neighbor downstairs cooks with a lot of onions, or maybe garlic, I can never tell the difference once it gets in the hallway.

But things other people don’t notice… I’m not sure. I haven’t had, like, a smell that nobody else can smell, if that’s what you mean.
Aside from the kitchen situation, have you been managing your usual daily activities the way you normally would?

Yes, mostly I do. I mean, the kitchen thing has thrown everything off a little, because when your house is being worked on you can’t put things where they go, and then you forget where you put the measuring cups—though my sister always said I owned too many anyway.

But outside of that, I still go to church gatherings, and I’ve kept up with book club. I do my usual things around the house, laundry and bills and all that, and I still make plans with my family like I normally would. So yes, I’d say I’m managing.
Have you been feeling unusually cheerful or high in mood?

Unusually cheerful? No, I wouldn’t say that. I have moments where I feel all right, you know, if the sun is out or if someone brings decent cake to church coffee hour—though half the time it’s too dry and people pretend it isn’t.

But high in mood, like more than normal? I don’t think so. I’m just… myself, I suppose. Some days better than others.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? No, I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes out of the corner of my eye I’ll think there’s a cat or something, but that’s usually just a sweater on a chair, and I’ve always been bad about leaving sweaters on chairs. My mother used to say if you put things away you won’t scare yourself half to death, and she was right about that.

But no, not like seeing something other people couldn’t see. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you had any recent seizures?

Seizures? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve never been one to faint or anything dramatic like that—well, except once years ago at a school assembly, but that was because it was hot and they made us stand too long, which was ridiculous.

But recently, no, I haven’t noticed anything like seizures.
Aside from the trouble with the contractor and neighbors, have you had any other strong beliefs that people say are not true?

Other beliefs? Well… I suppose it all comes back to that kitchen business, doesn’t it? I mean, people say, “Oh, it’s just a mistake,” or “contractors are always late,” but it’s been nearly two years, and you don’t keep making the same “mistake” unless there’s a reason.

The contractor and some people on my block, they’ve been working together somehow. Quietly. My husband shows me receipts and says it’s all accounted for, but receipts can say anything if someone knows what they’re doing. And the neighbors act like they don’t know, but then they make these little comments, you know, over the hedge or when the bins go out, and it’s always just enough to let me know.

So, no, not other things exactly. It’s that they’re cheating us and keeping the kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and everyone wants me to pretend I don’t see it.
Have you ever felt that something outside you was controlling your actions?

Controlling my actions? No, I don’t think so. I decide what I’m doing, like whether I’m going to call someone or check something or… well, half the time I walk into a room and forget why I went in there, but that’s just getting older, isn’t it?

I don’t feel like a puppet or anything like that, if that’s what you mean. I get upset, sure, and then I might do more than I planned, like making lists or going back over things, but that’s still me doing it.
Did these suspicions begin after you started any new medication?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t remember starting anything new right before all this. I mean, I’ve had the usual sort of things doctors give you over the years, and half the time the labels are so tiny you need a magnifying glass—my husband bought one for the junk drawer and then of course nobody puts it back where it belongs.

But no, I can’t say I noticed, like, “Oh, I started a pill and then the suspicions began.” It didn’t feel like that to me.
Have you been neglecting your personal hygiene, like bathing or changing clothes less often than usual?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I still get myself ready and go to church gatherings, and my book club too—though last time we picked a book I could barely stand, everyone raved about it and I thought, well, maybe I missed something.

But I’m still doing my usual things around the house, keeping up with family plans, that sort of thing. I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped taking care of myself.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are first-rank psychotic symptoms that would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or psychosis due to a medical condition.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that something outside you was controlling your actions?

target_item.reason: The question asks about experiences of outside control over one's actions, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles or manifestations.

patient.answer:
Controlling my actions? No, I don’t think so. I decide what I’m doing, like whether I’m going to call someone or check something or… well, half the time I walk into a room and forget why I went in there, but that’s just getting older, isn’t it?

I don’t feel like a puppet or anything like that, if that’s what you mean. I get upset, sure, and then I might do more than I planned, like making lists or going back over things, but that’s still me doing it.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t remember starting anything new right before all this. I mean, I’ve had the usual sort of things doctors give you over the years, and half the time the labels are so tiny you need a magnifying glass—my husband bought one for the junk drawer and then of course nobody puts it back where it belongs.

But no, I can’t say I noticed, like, “Oh, I started a pill and then the suspicions began.” It didn’t feel like that to me.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I still get myself ready and go to church gatherings, and my book club too—though last time we picked a book I could barely stand, everyone raved about it and I thought, well, maybe I missed something.

But I’m still doing my usual things around the house, keeping up with family plans, that sort of thing. I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped taking care of myself.
